model: Sum-of-parts: consolidated-operations owner-FCF DCF plus associates and joint ventures at book (engine route)

inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5% in HKD, unchanged from the prior version: HK long bond (tracks USD under the peg, ~4.0-4.3%) plus ~4.5-5.0pp equity risk premium for a mature, diversified but geopolitically exposed group. ONE WACC across all three scenarios -- risk is charged in the scenario flows and the weights, not in the rate (the prior file said this but ran the bull case at 8.0%; corrected to 8.5%).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) -- leases as an operating cost. CHANGED from the prior version, which used (A). Reason: lease cash cost is HK$17.8bn a year (FY2025 principal 14,839 + interest 2,993; H1 FY2026 7,390 + 1,447) against a lease liability of only HK$63.5bn, because A.S. Watson store leases are short and renew indefinitely. Treatment (A) therefore charged ~3.6 years of a perpetual cost and no renewal line -- roughly neither. Now: ebitda_margin_path is the POST-IFRS-16 underlying EBITDA of the Company and subsidiaries, lease_cost_pct_path deducts the full cash lease payment (principal + interest), da_pct_path is PRE-IFRS-16 D&A (ex right-of-use depreciation: H1 FY2026 11,416 of 18,472), and lease liabilities (HK$63,492m) are EXCLUDED from net debt and from the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted ONCE, as a stock in the equity bridge at 30-Jun-2026 book (HK$130,909m, which includes perpetual capital securities issued by subsidiaries). CHANGED from the prior version, which deducted nothing on the mistaken premise that consolidated cash flow is net of minorities -- it is not: consolidated OCF is 100% of every subsidiary and minorities are paid in financing (dividends to NCI HK$5,053m FY2025; NCI + perps profit share HK$7.5bn). Flows here are 100%-consolidated and unlevered. Book is a fair-to-slightly-conservative proxy: NCI takes roughly 35% of consolidated-operations earnings (PSA 20% of Hutchison Ports plus terminal-level minorities, Temasek 25% of A.S. Watson, 34% of HTHKH) and 24.3% of CKI; capitalising that on this model’s own values gives ~HK$115-137bn.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum-of-parts on the engine route, the same pattern as 1113.HK. (1) Consolidated operations (A.S. Watson retail, consolidated ports, 3 Group Europe ex-UK, HTHKH, corporate) are valued by an unlevered component owner-FCF DCF built from the EBITDA of the Company and subsidiaries only. (2) Associates and joint ventures (CKI’s infrastructure portfolio, Cenovus, HPH Trust, port and retail JVs, HUTCHMED, IOH etc.) go into the equity bridge at 30-Jun-2026 book, and their dividends are NOT in the flows (matching-asset rule). (3) The 49% VodafoneThree stake, held for sale at 30-Jun-2026 and sold 30-Jul-2026, is taken at its cash proceeds. (4) Less net debt, NCI at book, pension deficit and the interim dividend paid after the balance sheet. The SKILL.md holdco row (BVPS x exit P/B) was rejected because two-fifths of the value is controlled operating cash flow; a pure owner-FCF DCF was rejected because half the group’s EBITDA (H1 FY2026 pre-IFRS-16: 42.2bn of 80.2bn) sits in associates/JVs that never touch consolidated EBITDA. WHY THE PRIOR VERSION WAS REBUILT: it ran the engine on the Metrics.csv EBITDA (77,325) and ~27% margin, which is not the consolidated-subsidiaries figure (FY2025 EBITDA of Company and subsidiaries 57,351 reported, ~67bn underlying incl. five months of 3 UK); it deducted leases at liability value only; it deducted nothing for NCI; it deducted the HK$3.9bn NCI shareholder loans twice (they are already inside the HK$67,510m net debt); and it omitted the GBP4.3bn VodafoneThree proceeds received after the balance-sheet date. CALIBRATION (FY2026E = year 1): H1 FY2026 EBITDA of Company and subsidiaries 46,630 less disposal gains 16,669 plus the non-cash 2,844 acquisition-premium write-off = 32,805 underlying post-IFRS-16 (24.0% of 136,485 revenue); lease cash 8,837 (6.5%); pre-IFRS-16 D&A 11,416 (8.4%); capex = fixed assets 6,271 + licences 364 + brand/other rights 780 + capitalised customer acquisition costs 1,953 = 9,368 in H1, second-half weighted (FY2025 ex-UK ~22bn) -> 7.8% of revenue; tax paid 2,853 = ~21.5% of lease-adjusted EBIT. Cross-check from the cash flow statement: H1 FY2026 FFO 36,213 - dividends from associates/JVs 14,449 + interest paid 6,005 - lease principal and interest 8,837 - capex 7,415 = HK$11.5bn unlevered consolidated FCF in the half, against a modelled HK$21.6bn for the year. Attributable tie: year-1 NOPAT ~21bn - after-tax interest ~7bn + underlying share of associate/JV profit ~20bn - NCI ~7.5bn = ~26bn vs H1 FY2026 underlying profit 12,580 x 2. PERIMETER: FY2025 revenue of 280,036 included 3 UK to end-May 2025 and Panama; H1 FY2026 revenue 136,485 excludes 3 UK entirely and Panama from late February, so year-1 growth is +0.5% reported (~+5% like-for-like, helped by EUR). UKPN and UK Rail left the JV balance before 30-Jun-2026, and their proceeds are in the 30-Jun-2026 cash. PANAMA: out of the flows; the ICC claim (>US$2bn) is memo-only upside, not capitalised. NOT MODELLED: a holding-company discount. Associates and JVs are at full book in all three scenarios (the engine carries one bridge), supported by UKPN and VodafoneThree both selling above carrying value, but the stock has traded at 0.35-0.5x book for years; see valuation_philosophy. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped -- the group is in net debt and the DCF is unlevered. BUYBACKS: none since FY2022; count flat by fact, not convention. The Metrics.csv total_debt (330,089 FY2025) does not reconcile to the filing and was not used.

This is a memo of what reached ordinary shareholders; the DCF flows are a different (unlevered, consolidated-subsidiaries-only) stream -- see notes.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr, cross-checked against the company's own underlying-profit growth (+7% FY2024->FY2025, excluding one-off items) and near-flat FY2020-2025 revenue CAGR (~1.0%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Reported EPS/net-income CAGR (-15% to -31%) diverges sharply from revenue and equity CAGRs (~1-2%) but is a false signal: FY2025 net income was cut by a HK$10,469m NON-CASH UK-merger loss and FY2024 by a HK$3,740m non-cash Vietnam-telecom impairment, neither of which touches cash flow or FCF (FCF CAGR 3yr +10%, 5yr roughly flat). Growth rate is anchored on revenue/equity/underlying-profit, not on the impairment-distorted reported-EPS series.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs are on the reported series (SBC is zero, so reported FCF = SBC-adjusted FCF). Reported FCF is OCF less fixed-asset capex: it includes ~HK$12bn a year of associate/JV dividends and is before HK$14.8bn of lease principal and HK$5bn of NCI dividends, so it is not the valuation base (FY2025 unlevered consolidated-operations FCF after leases was ~HK$19bn).

base.narrative: Consolidated operations only (retail, consolidated ports, 3 Group Europe ex-UK, HTHKH). Year 1 is FY2026: reported revenue +0.5% as the UK telecom and Panama exits offset ~5% like-for-like growth; thereafter the prior 2% path, unchanged. Underlying post-IFRS-16 margin of the Company and subsidiaries held flat at the H1 FY2026 level of 24% -- retail growth and telecom cost-cutting offset by mix shift toward thin-margin retail, as in the prior version’s flat-margin judgment. Full lease cash cost charged at 6.4% of revenue; capex including licences, brands and capitalised customer acquisition costs at 7.8%, roughly equal to pre-IFRS-16 D&A. Capital recycling is in the anchors (net debt, VodafoneThree proceeds), not the flows.

bull.narrative: A.S. Watson's dual HK/London IPO (targeting ~US$30bn valuation) proceeds and lands on schedule, crystallising retail value and funding growth/buybacks; VodafoneThree synergies and European telecom in-market consolidation lift telecom margins faster than base case; Cenovus (post-MEG Energy) and other Finance & Investments associates deliver stronger commodity-price-driven contributions; the stalled non-Panama global ports consortium sale (BlackRock/MSC/COSCO) eventually completes at a full price (the engine carries one bridge, so this shows up as higher consolidated margins and growth rather than a disposal gain), crystallising further value and de-risking the geopolitical overhang; successful Panama arbitration recovery is a memo-only upside not included in these cash flows.

bear.narrative: Continued national-security/geopolitical scrutiny of ports and telecom (Panama-style concession risk resurfaces elsewhere), the non-Panama global ports consortium sale stays stalled indefinitely denying value crystallisation, global trade growth slows further pressuring ports throughput, European telecom stays a low-return, capital-intensive, price-competitive industry limiting VodafoneThree synergy realisation, and A.S. Watson's IPO slips repeatedly (now flagged to 2027) or prices well below the targeted ~US$30bn, denying the value-crystallisation catalyst. Retail margins compress further under e-commerce and cost pressure, consistent with the segment's structurally thin ~9% EBITDA margin. Risk is charged in these flows, not by raising WACC above base -- a single flat 8.5% WACC is used across scenarios per the house rule against charging risk twice.

scenario_narratives.base: Consolidated operations compound at ~2% on a flat 24% underlying margin after full lease cost; associates and JVs are held at book; the balance sheet carries the UKPN, UK Rail and VodafoneThree proceeds. Panama is out of the flows and its arbitration claim is not capitalised.
scenario_narratives.bull: A.S. Watson IPO crystallises retail value on schedule, VodafoneThree and Cenovus outperform, the stalled global ports consortium sale eventually completes at full value.
scenario_narratives.bear: Geopolitical/national-security risk to ports and telecom concessions resurfaces beyond Panama, the ports consortium sale stays stalled, European telecom stays low-return, and the A.S. Watson IPO catalyst slips or disappoints -- growth stalls and margin compresses on structural retail mix shift.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 30/45/25 from the prior version. Bear 30% (above the 15% default): several live, binary geopolitical/regulatory risks sit on headline assets -- the stalled ports consortium sale, national-security scrutiny beyond Panama, low-return European telecom -- and no new evidence since September resolves any of them (no Panama ruling, no ports deal, no A.S. Watson decision). Bull 25%: it needs several things to go right together (A.S. Watson listing at target, ports sale completing, telecom and Cenovus outperformance). Base 45%. Evidence that would move them: a Panama award or settlement, a signed and approved ports sale, or an A.S. Watson prospectus (bull up); a second concession loss or a failed ports deal (bear up).

entry_price.note: OVERSTATED as a 15% buy-below price: the engine re-discounts the operating flows at the hurdle but carries the equity bridge at face, and here the bridge is +HK$50/share net (associates and JVs at book, which earn ~7% on book and pay ~4.5% in dividends). A buyer demanding 15% would not pay book for them. Re-pricing the associates/JVs and the matching minority share at the hurdle puts a self-consistent entry price very roughly in the HK$45-50 range -- an estimate outside the engine, not a model output.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CK Hutchison is valued as the sum of two things it actually owns: controlled operating cash flow (an unlevered owner-FCF DCF on the EBITDA of the Company and subsidiaries, after the full cash cost of leases), and non-controlled stakes (associates and joint ventures at book, with their dividends kept out of the flows so nothing is counted twice). The VodafoneThree stake is taken at the cash received on 30-Jul-2026. Net debt, minorities at book, the pension deficit and the post-balance-sheet interim dividend come off. SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street coincide. MEMO, no-re-rate reference: no holding-company discount is applied, and this is the assumption the market most plainly rejects -- the shares have traded at roughly 0.35-0.5x ordinary shareholders’ funds for years (book HK$151/share at 30-Jun-2026, so ~HK$53-76 on the stock’s own range), and management has said disposal proceeds will be redeployed rather than returned. The gap between that range and the scenario values is the price of the re-rating thesis; the 15% hurdle entry price is the figure that does not depend on it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Holding-company discount persists: associates and JVs (HK$284bn, HK$74/share) are carried at full book in every scenario, and retained disposal proceeds are redeployed at returns near or below the cost of equity instead of being distributed
Bear case is not bearish on the bridge: a further Panama-style concession loss or an associate impairment would hit book values the engine holds constant across scenarios
Minorities are deducted at book (HK$131bn); if terminal-level port minorities and Temasek’s A.S. Watson stake are worth more than book, attributable value is lower
Further concession or regulatory losses beyond Panama (ports and telecom treated as national-security assets)
The ~US$22.8bn non-Panama ports consortium sale stays stalled or fails; the A.S. Watson listing (targeted ~US$30bn) slips further or prices below target
Structural retail margin compression and a low-return, capex-heavy European telecom footprint keep consolidated FCF conversion poor (capex ~ D&A, FCF ~8% of revenue)
Leadership succession as the Li Ka-shing-era executives retire after the divestment programme
